title: Silverpine Cayman Feeder IV — Joint Non-US Signer W-8BEN-E Deadlock
fund: Silverpine Heritage Cayman Feeder IV, L.P. (Cayman master-feeder)
initialRequestBrief: Silverpine Heritage is launching Silverpine Heritage Cayman Feeder IV, L.P., a CIMA-registered exempted limited partnership feeding into its Master Fund IV, with an initial close of 23 April 2025. The LP base is mostly non-US institutional entities completing IRS Form W-8BEN-E plus a CRS entity self-certification, and many of them execute through two or three joint authorised signers under board resolutions. Harbourline Fund Services (Cayman) is administrator and will review every tax form before acceptance. Fund counsel's final-form subscription agreement (Section 4.3 and Annex B) allocates the tax elections to a single Designated Tax Signatory. We need the five-step SubFlow flow, including joint-signer routing and SignVault envelopes, live for UAT by 7 April.
summary: Joint-signer non-US entities deadlocked at Step 4 (Tax Certifications) when a co-signer reviewed the Passive NFFE branch while the primary signer elected Active NFFE. The v2 schema gave the Chapter 4 and CRS elections to the Designated Tax Signatory only, evaluated rules on committed state and split SignVault anchors per recipient.
howItWent: UAT sign-off was due on 15 April when QA found that joint accounts froze on "Waiting for other signers" at Step 4. 14 of the 31 initial-close LPs (about US$212M of commitments) were non-US institutions with two joint signers, and all 14 sat at 98% completion. Signer A elected Active NFFE on W-8BEN-E line 5 while Co-Signer B, whose draft had been prefilled as Passive NFFE from the CRS self-certification, was still reviewing Part XXIX; the v1 step lock and draft-based rules left each waiting on the other. A forced unlock then failed envelope pre-flight on a duplicated Chapter 4 anchor. Minh Nguyen found the root cause the same night and shipped the v2 schema by 00:14, but the administrator had to re-run its joint-signer UAT over the Cayman Easter holidays. UAT sign-off and the initial close each slipped 9 days, to 24 April and 2 May. No LP ever signed a v1 W-8BEN-E, so nothing had to be re-papered.
resolutionSteps: Isolate tax entity classification to the PRIMARY_TAX_COLLABORATOR role, mapped from the Annex B Designated Tax Signatory; co-signers get a read-only view of W-8BEN-E line 5, Parts XXV/XXVI/XXIX and the CRS classification.
Evaluate every visibleWhen/requiredWhen rule against committed state, and key Part XXIX on the committed Chapter 4 election and line 40c choice.
Replace the step-wide exclusive lock with a completion rule: valid committed tax data plus one Annex B attestation per co-signer.

Decouple co-signer signature routing: the primary signs W-8BEN-E Part XXX at \ch4_primary_sig\ and each co-signer signs only the Annex B acknowledgement at \cosigner_N_attest\, so co-signers never re-trigger Chapter 4 status resets.
Remove the CRS-to-FATCA prefill and turn a FATCA/CRS classification mismatch into an administrator warning.
Reset all v1 UAT drafts and re-run the administrator's joint-signer UAT with concurrent sessions in both signer orders.

pitfalls.warning: Never let more than one joint signer edit the Chapter 4 election. If two signers on one account can see different Part XXIX visibility, the schema is wrong.
pitfalls.author: minh.nguyen

pitfalls.warning: Hiding Part XXIX for joint accounts is not a workaround: a Passive NFFE must tick line 40b or list owners on line 40c, and the administrator will bounce every incomplete W-8BEN-E.
pitfalls.author: minh.nguyen

pitfalls.warning: Single-tester UAT (one person driving each signer in turn) cannot reproduce the co-signer-first deadlock. Use concurrent sessions in both signer orders.
pitfalls.author: sarah.tran

pitfalls.warning: A role-model change after UAT starts forces the administrator to re-run its script; budget extra administrator UAT days, more around Cayman public holidays.
pitfalls.author: chloe.nguyen

artifacts.description: Operations playbook for joint non-US institutional signers on Cayman feeders: role mapping at kickoff, build rules, concurrent-session UAT script and go-live gates.
16 joint-signer scenarios (Chapter 4 status x CRS class x signer count x who opens Step 4 first) with expected v2 behaviour, v1 result and administrator review outcome.

State-isolated Step 4 form routing rule: the Designated Tax Signatory owns Chapter 4 and CRS elections, rules evaluate on committed state, co-signers attest per Annex B, SignVault anchors split per recipient.
Subscription agreement excerpt: Cayman AML, FATCA/CRS reporting, Section 4.3 Designated Tax Signatory, Annex B designation and the Schedule A tax certification matrix.
Timeline, root cause, the v2 fix, the 9-day impact and six reusable rules for joint-signer tax flows.
